name: home-hero
description:
The full-bleed video stage: the 4K first frame is the poster so a crisp still is on screen the instant the page paints, the muted loop fades in once it can play, and a scrim carries light copy over bright footage. The stage is dark in either theme — its ground is the FOOTAGE, not a colour, which is why the contrast gate is pointed at the composited pixels via `data-ground="media"` on the content wrapper.

The scrim's three stops are TOKENS, not percentages written at a call site. They were 50/32/55 of marine mixed in page CSS, which is how the top stop came to be measurably unable to carry white nav ink over the video's sky (2.99:1 where the links need 4.5). The guarantee lives in `--color-scrim-strong` now; raising it fixes every surface that floats text on media. The middle stop is `--color-scrim-heavy` (55%) — the lightest stop that holds: 45% measured 2.99:1 behind the display line, a hundredth under the 3:1 it needs, in exactly the place every gate reports as 'sits on imagery, check by eye'.

The one deliberate exception in this unit: `min-height: 85vh` and the `12vh` clamp term. The stage is the viewport's opening frame — the box it sizes against IS the window — so the viewport unit is measuring the right box, the same reasoning nav-menu records for its `vw`.

base.$description: Its own container: the heading's 6.5cqi clamp measures this stage. `isolation: isolate` keeps the negative z-index video and scrim inside the section's own stacking context instead of behind the page.

& [data-emph='past'].$description: On the photograph the page inks do not apply: everything here is the light ink, and `past` is that ink held back.

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).$description: With the video hidden, the poster still shows via the section's own background so the stage is never blank.

media.$description: The video cannot be a view node (SAFE_TAGS admits no `<video>`), so it arrives through the render seam inside this wrapper — which dissolves, so the video's absolute inset still resolves against the section.

scrim.$description: Slightly stronger at top and bottom, lighter through the middle where the scene reads — enough to carry white text, not enough to flatten it. The top stop is the documented guarantee for the nav links over the video's sky; dropping it re-breaks exactly the bug the unit description records.

a11y.note: The video and scrim are `aria-hidden` decoration behind a real `<h1>`; under `prefers-reduced-motion` the video is removed entirely and the poster takes its place, so nothing moves and nothing is lost. The content wrapper carries `data-ground="media"` so the contrast gate measures the composited pixels the copy actually sits on.
